data.expected_signal: max_ratio > 1 (tolerance violation) on near-cancelling legal inputs

evidence.summary: On 100k worst-cancelled rows selected from 4M random full-range FP16 inputs (cancellation ratio down to 2.0e-7), max error/tolerance ratio was 0.298 with zero violations; benign inputs gave 0.285. The hypothesized catastrophic cancellation does not occur because a*c and b*d are exact in fp32 (11+11 bit mantissas), so the fp32 round-to-nearest sum has error relative to the small result (≤ ulp(rn)/2), not the large operands; div_rn adds one more 2^-24 relative rounding. Total relative error stays well under the 5e-7 tolerance.

data.expected_signal: max_ratio > 1, non-finite output, or inputs not preserved on corner-case legal inputs

evidence.summary: Corner-case probe over extrema (±65504), subnormals, signed zeros, and shared-backing-storage contiguous views: 20000 rows, zero tolerance violations (max ratio 0.186), all outputs finite, shared-view case max ratio 0.243 with 0 violations, and inputs preserved. No legal-domain corner case violates the contract.

rationale: Products of fp16 values are exact in fp32, but the sum/subtraction of two large products that nearly cancel rounds at ulp(large operand), so the absolute error in the numerator can be ~2^-24*|a*c|, which after division by a small c*c+d*d yields an error far exceeding 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| when the true component is small (catastrophic cancellation), e.g. large-magnitude a,b with near-cancelling products.

scope_evidence.summary: The contract declares 'EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and both extrema' and requires 'abs(actual - target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7 * abs(target)' per component, with 'A small real component must meet its own tolerance even when the imaginary component is large'.

scope_rationale: The contract requires every finite FP16 component combination to meet abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7+5e-7*|target| per component; an input with large a,b and near-cancelling products is explicitly legal, so an accuracy failure there violates the required tolerance.
statement: The kernel's fp32 intermediate arithmetic (real_numerator = a*c + b*d, imag_numerator = b*c - a*d computed in float32) produces componentwise errors exceeding the contract tolerance 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target| for legal FP16 inputs where the two products nearly cancel.
